_: Bonitz's own list of work sigla, VERIFIED against the 1870 original at 400 dpi
on 2026-08-08: archive.org `aristotelisopera05arisuoft`, leaf n263.
(Printed p. VII, the EDITOR sigla — Bk, Bz, Did — is leaf n260; do not confuse
the two lists. The front matter is not in work/scan400/, which starts at 015.)
A citation siglum is WORK + BOOK NUMERAL: `Ζιι` is Ζι (Historia animalium)
plus book ι, `Ζμβ` is Ζμ plus book β, `πκγ` is π (Problemata) plus κγ = 23.
So the vowels inside a siglum are accounted for in exactly two ways — as part
of the work siglum itself (αι, ακ, αν, αρ, ατ, εν, ε, ηε, ημ, ο, υ ...) or as
a Greek alphabetic book numeral. Anything else is a misread siglum, and until
now nothing checked: the `siglum` and `label` guards exempt ANY siglum-shaped
token, so `Ζιι` correctly escapes and a corrupted `Ζμ`/`Ζυ` escapes with it.
That is the `Ζιβ28` failure of 2026-08-06, where all three readers were wrong
and no check fired.
Case is significant and is Bonitz's own: Ζι vs ζ, Μ vs μ, Ο vs ο, Π vs π,
Ρ vs ρ, Φ vs φ, Κ vs κ are all DIFFERENT works.
⚠ THE LIST IS NOT A DICTIONARY. `ζ` names TWO title-lines — περὶ Ζωῆς ϗ
θανάτȣ and περὶ Νεότητος ϗ γήρως — so 48 printed rows carry 47 distinct
sigla. The list is alphabetised by TITLE, which is why the two ζ rows sit far
apart. This corrects the earlier reading `ν` for περὶ Νεότητος, which was a
300 dpi guess from the work's name: at 400 dpi the glyph is a zeta, identical
to the ζ of περὶ Ζωῆς and nothing like the ν of μν directly above it. The two
works are contiguous in Bekker (both inside Juv, 467b-480b), so a range check
is unaffected by the ambiguity — but a parser keyed by siglum is not.
`bekker` is the Bekker page range. `manifest` names the file in the wider
repo's manifests/ that is the authority for it — those carry first/last
column AND per-book ranges, and build/dist/<id>/chapters.json carries
per-chapter spans. Entries with "source": "hand" are NOT in the repo and
were entered from standard Bekker pagination; a check must stay silent on
them until they are verified, or it will manufacture false errors the way
bekker.py's guessed table did (103 of them).
⚠ THE BIGGEST TRAP FOR A RANGE CHECK: a bare book letter inherits the
previous citation's work. Verified 2026-08-08 by page number — `Ζιε13.
544a32. ζ1. 558b13` is HA book 6, `Ηζ2. 1139b9. ζ4. 1140a19` is EN book 6,
`Πδ15. 1299a8. ζ2. 1317b41` is Politics book 6. 29 of the 40 bare-ζ tokens
in the corpus are this, not the work ζ. A checker that reads them as work
sigla condemns every one. Resolve the inherited work from the preceding
citation BEFORE testing any Bekker page.
OPEN: two rows — αι and Μ — print a small `i e` between siglum and title.
Unexplained; look at it before writing the citation parser.
